paths.description: Landing/feed template and global navigation; tested desktop, mobile, dark, contrast, reduced motion, network, performance, security, crawler and memory conditions.
Representative OGV title detail from the published sitemap; covers entity content, metadata, localized detail layout, and no-JS rendering.
Representative OGV playback route from the sitemap; covers region/rights failure and recovery state.
Representative user-generated video route from the sitemap; covers player-first content and muted autoplay surface.

findings.summary: The light surface remains white under prefers-color-scheme: dark
findings.evidence: The light surface remains white under prefers-color-scheme: dark; DOM reports color-scheme: normal and the CSS probe found no prefers-color-scheme rules.
findings.suggestedFix: Add color-scheme: light dark and theme surfaces with prefers-color-scheme or light-dark().

findings.summary: The prefers-contrast: more capture is visually unchanged from the default, and the CSS probe found no site-level contrast adaptation.
findings.evidence: The prefers-contrast: more capture is visually unchanged from the default, and the CSS probe found no site-level contrast adaptation.
findings.suggestedFix: Add forced-colors and prefers-contrast adjustments for essential controls and muted text.

findings.summary: The CSS probe found no view-transition declarations
findings.evidence: The CSS probe found no view-transition declarations; route and state changes use abrupt custom panels.
findings.suggestedFix: Use same-document and cross-document View Transitions for menu, sign-in, and route changes, with reduced-motion handling.

findings.summary: The CSS probe found no scroll-snap, overscroll, or declarative gesture treatment, while the long card feed is touch-centric.
findings.evidence: The CSS probe found no scroll-snap, overscroll, or declarative gesture treatment, while the long card feed is touch-centric.
findings.suggestedFix: Use native scrolling, overscroll behavior, and scroll snap where carousels or gesture navigation require it instead of custom pointer handling.

findings.summary: The fixed header remains static while scrolling a page over 7,000 CSS pixels tall
findings.evidence: The fixed header remains static while scrolling a page over 7,000 CSS pixels tall; DOM/CSS evidence found no scroll-state query or progress cue.
findings.suggestedFix: Make the fixed chrome respond to scroll state and add a lightweight progress or shrinking-header treatment.

findings.summary: The sign-in panel is a custom overlay with no dialog/popover or anchor-positioning primitive
findings.evidence: The sign-in panel is a custom overlay with no dialog/popover or anchor-positioning primitive; on mobile it is clipped beyond the right edge.
findings.suggestedFix: Use popover plus CSS anchor positioning and fallback positions for the sign-in panel.

findings.summary: The open sign-in panel covers content without focus treatment or a directional transition, and the probe found no view-transition or highlight support.
findings.evidence: The open sign-in panel covers content without focus treatment or a directional transition, and the probe found no view-transition or highlight support.
findings.suggestedFix: Guide attention with managed focus and a directional transition when opening navigation or account panels.

findings.summary: On desktop the cookie banner consumes about one-third of the viewport
findings.evidence: On desktop the cookie banner consumes about one-third of the viewport; on mobile it covers the lower portion while the sign-in panel simultaneously obscures the content.
findings.suggestedFix: Replace the oversized load-time banner with a compact, accessible consent surface that does not obscure core content.

findings.summary: The probe found zero dialog, popover, and details elements even though a sign-in overlay and cookie consent surface are visible.
findings.evidence: The probe found zero dialog, popover, and details elements even though a sign-in overlay and cookie consent surface are visible.
findings.suggestedFix: Use dialog for modal consent and popover for transient account UI, with declarative dismiss and focus behavior.

findings.summary: The cookie banner and sign-in panel dominate the first viewport and obscure the media experience.
findings.evidence: The cookie banner and sign-in panel dominate the first viewport and obscure the media experience.
findings.suggestedFix: Reduce persistent chrome and defer account promotion until user intent is expressed.

findings.summary: The CSS probe found no container queries despite reusable card, header, and account-panel components appearing at desktop and mobile sizes.
findings.evidence: The CSS probe found no container queries despite reusable card, header, and account-panel components appearing at desktop and mobile sizes.
findings.suggestedFix: Add container-type to reusable card/panel regions and adapt them with size-aware container queries.

findings.summary: 80 of 201 visible controls measured below 24px in at least one dimension
findings.evidence: 80 of 201 visible controls measured below 24px in at least one dimension; sampled controls had no visible computed outline, including unnamed 24px buttons.
findings.suggestedFix: Increase targets to at least 44 CSS pixels where practical and provide clear :focus-visible styles and non-hover fallbacks.

findings.summary: The sitemap-listed play page for /play/34450 dead-ends with a rights-holder availability message
findings.evidence: The sitemap-listed play page for /play/34450 dead-ends with a rights-holder availability message; the account panel and consent banner obscure the recovery action.
findings.suggestedFix: Keep unavailable-title recovery visible and offer clear alternative episodes or region-available recommendations without overlapping overlays.

findings.summary: The play page shows an availability error, but overlapping account and cookie UI hides context and makes the single recovery action hard to understand.
findings.evidence: The play page shows an availability error, but overlapping account and cookie UI hides context and makes the single recovery action hard to understand.
findings.suggestedFix: Present an explicit, unobscured error state with retry, back, and alternative-content actions.

findings.evidence: Lighthouse measured landing-page LCP 14.4s and CLS 0.737; the direct trace measured LCP 3.98s and mobile layout measured CLS 0.496, all outside good thresholds.

findings.evidence: The anonymous landing state retained about 460,279 heap nodes and 32.55MB self size before interaction, a large baseline for a feed whose first viewport is mostly cards and chrome.
findings.suggestedFix: Reduce eager framework/player/identity allocations and lazy-initialize offscreen feed and player features.

taskList.title: Add HSTS, CSP, nosniff, framing protection, Referrer-Policy and Permissions-Policy; set Secure and appropriate SameSite cookies.
Prioritize the LCP candidate, reserve dynamic content space, and defer non-critical work.
Give icon controls accessible names and preserve semantic roles for all interactive elements.
Present equally clear accept, reject, and manage choices and defer optional tracking until consent.
Server-render the landing feed and navigation so core discovery remains useful without JavaScript.
Replace the oversized load-time banner with a compact, accessible consent surface that does not obscure core content.
Emit responsive srcset/sizes and intrinsic dimensions, retaining modern formats and right-sized variants.
Use real href values and descriptive names for links, and serve a valid text/plain robots.txt.
Add container-type to reusable card/panel regions and adapt them with size-aware container queries.
Reduce eager framework/player/identity allocations and lazy-initialize offscreen feed and player features.
